extracted.intended_audience: patent litigators, patent attorneys, parties in U.S. patent litigation, and courts
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of statutory standards governing the presumption of patent validity and the defenses available and pleading/notice requirements in U.S. patent litigation under 35 U.S.C. § 282.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of validity
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent shall be presumed valid. Each claim of a patent (whether in independent, dependent, or multiple dependent form) shall be presumed valid independently of the validity of other claims; dependent or multiple dependent claims shall be presumed valid even though dependent upon an invalid claim. The burden of establishing invalidity of a patent or any claim thereof shall rest on the party asserting such invalidity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory rule placing the burden of proof for invalidity on the party asserting it and treating each claim's validity independently. Use when assessing who must prove invalidity and whether dependent claims survive invalidation of another claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defenses must be pleaded
rubrics_metrics.description: The following shall be defenses in any action involving the validity or infringement of a patent and shall be pleaded:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory requirement that defenses be asserted in the pleadings. Failure to plead a defense may have procedural consequences; specific defenses listed in the statute follow this introductory requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense — Noninfringement, absence of liability, or unenforceability
rubrics_metrics.description: Noninfringement, absence of liability for infringement or unenforceability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are enumerated, generally-available defenses in infringement/validity actions. 'Unenforceability' covers equitable defenses (e.g., inequitable conduct) subject to other applicable law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense — Invalidity on statutory grounds (Part II conditions for patentability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Invalidity of the patent or any claim in suit on any ground specified in part II as a condition for patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers classic patentability challenges (e.g., novelty, nonobviousness, written description where applicable) as defined elsewhere in Title 35 (Part II). Such invalidity defenses must be pleaded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense — Invalidity for failure to comply with section 112 (with best-mode exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: Invalidity of the patent or any claim in suit for failure to comply with any requirement of section 112, except that the failure to disclose the best mode shall not be a basis on which any claim of a patent may be canceled or held invalid or otherwise unenforceable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 112-related defects (e.g., lack of written description, lack of enablement, indefiniteness) are recognized invalidity defenses, but the specific 'best mode' failure is expressly not a basis for invalidating or cancelling a claim under this statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense — Invalidity for failure to comply with section 251
rubrics_metrics.description: Invalidity of the patent or any claim in suit for failure to comply with any requirement of section 251.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 251 concerns reissued patents; failure to meet its requirements may be raised as an invalidity defense and must be pleaded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense — Any other Title 35 fact or act made a defense
rubrics_metrics.description: Any other fact or act made a defense by this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catch-all allowing defenses that are created elsewhere in Title 35 to be raised in actions involving validity or infringement. Indicates statute is not exhaustive of possible defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirement for asserting invalidity or noninfringement
rubrics_metrics.description: In an action involving the validity or infringement of a patent the party asserting invalidity or noninfringement shall give notice in the pleadings or otherwise in writing to the adverse party at least thirty days before the trial, of the country, number, date, and name of the patentee of any patent, the title, date, and page numbers of any publication to be relied upon as anticipation of the patent in suit or ... as showing the state of the art, and the name and address of any person who may be relied upon as the prior inventor or as having prior knowledge of or as having previously used or offered for sale the invention of the patent in suit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific pre-trial disclosure requirement: provide identifying information for patents, publications, and persons relied upon. If such notice is not given, proof of those matters may not be admitted at trial except on terms the court requires. Applies except in actions in the U.S. Court of Federal Claims (per statutory text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense — Invalidity of patent-term extension for material failure to comply with section 154(b) or 156
rubrics_metrics.description: Invalidity of the extension of a patent term or any portion thereof under section 154(b) or 156 because of the material failure—(1) by the applicant for the extension, or (2) by the Director, to comply with the requirements of such section shall be a defense in any action involving the infringement of a patent during the period of the extension of its term and shall be pleaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows challenging the validity of an extension of patent term (e.g., PTA/PTE) in infringement proceedings when the extension resulted from material noncompliance by the applicant or the Director. Must be pleaded as a defense in the action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-reviewability of due diligence determination under section 156(d)(2) in such actions
rubrics_metrics.description: A due diligence determination under section 156(d)(2) is not subject to review in such an action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where extension invalidity can be pleaded, the statute bars judicial review of certain PTO due diligence determinations (section 156(d)(2)) within such infringement actions.
